notes: §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR3: "Identifier-3 must reference an elementary numeric integer." BindSetUpDown binds the UP BY/DOWN BY amount under OperandContext.ArithmeticIndexWindow, whose 2023 row admits an index-name and an index data item; the 85 gate GateCobol85IndexAmount/IsCobol85IndexAmount refuses a scaled numeric item, a non-integer literal, an expression, and (kb/Work PB5421) an index-name or a USAGE INDEX item, each COBOL0900 at 85 and accepted from 2002, where the amount is arithmetic-expression-2. Format 1's identifier-2 keeps admitting both (SR2). Accepted rightly: 99, S9(4), COMP, COMP-3, 9(18), 9PP, a subscripted integer.

next.reason: 1985: "Identifier-3 must reference an elementary numeric integer."; 2023: "No syntax rule of 14.9.39.3 constrains the UP BY/DOWN BY operand; the 2023 identifier-3 is an object-class receiving item.". The 2023 SET syntax rules shown never limit the UP BY/DOWN BY operand to an elementary numeric integer. The name identifier-3 now denotes an object reference, so the restriction is gone.
